introduction.text: Forte Trionfale is a historic fort in Rome, built in the late 19th century as part of the city’s defensive network. It later served as a military barracks and now houses municipal offices, reflecting its evolving role in Rome’s urban and military history.

history.description: Rome’s fortification system was expanded between 1877 and 1891, during which Forte Trionfale was planned.
Construction of Forte Trionfale began in 1882 and was completed in 1888 on Via Trionfale.
In 1907, Captain Arnaldo Ulivelli died in an aerostat accident on Via Cassia.
In 1921, the fort was used as a barracks for units of the Italian Army.
During the 1930s, an airship hangar was built to house dirigibles.
In the early 2000s, the fort was decommissioned by the Ministry of Defence.
In 2015, the City of Rome purchased the fort to serve as the new seat of Municipio Roma XIV and other public facilities.
